fixes.explanation: That's the answer, friend, and Amos doesn't dress it up. He says, "It will be darkness and not light." (Amos 5:18) These people long for the Day of the LORD, and Amos asks them straight out what it will be for them. Wishing hard for a day doesn't change what the day is.

Nice thought, but the house in this picture has no good news waiting. The man rests his hand against the wall, "…only to be bitten by a snake." (Amos 5:19) A snake is the answer, baker. Amos says the Day of the LORD will be like that.

Yes, and the LORD says it plainly: "I hate, I despise your feasts! I cannot stand the stench of your solemn assemblies." (Amos 5:21) Those are gatherings the people were holding, and the LORD says He cannot stand them. Then He keeps going, naming their offerings and their songs too. (Amos 5:22–23)

That would be a nice invitation, but it's not what He says. The LORD says, "I hate, I despise your feasts! I cannot stand the stench of your solemn assemblies." (Amos 5:21) He despises the feasts and cannot stand the assemblies, so wanting more of them isn't in this verse, baker.

That's the word. The LORD says, "But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream." (Amos 5:24) Justice is the river, and righteousness is the ever-flowing stream beside it. That's what He asks for, right after turning down the songs and the offerings.

Wisdom is a fine word, but it isn't the one here. The LORD says, "But let justice roll on like a river…" (Amos 5:24) The river He pictures is justice, friend. Righteousness comes right behind it as an ever-flowing stream.

Right on, friend. The LORD says, "You have taken along Sakkuth your king and Kaiwan your star god, the idols you made for yourselves." (Amos 5:26) Notice who made them: the people did. Their king and their star god, and the LORD calls both idols.

I can see why that one slipped in, with offerings on the LORD's mind. But the passage never mentions altars here. He says Sakkuth and Kaiwan are "…the idols you made for yourselves." (Amos 5:26) Sakkuth is called their king and Kaiwan their star god.

A new king is a fair guess, but that's not in this verse. The LORD says, "Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Damascus…" (Amos 5:27) Exile is the answer, baker, and it's a heavy one. The one speaking is the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.
